science.title: Transcription factor PgNAC72 activates DAMMARENEDIOL SYNTHASE expression to promote ginseng saponin biosynthesis.
science.description: The article focuses on the identification and functional characterization of PgNAC72, a methyl jasmonate (MeJA)-responsive NAC transcription factor in Panax ginseng, which promotes ginsenoside biosynthesis. PgNAC72 is predominantly expressed in ginseng flowers, localizes to the nucleus, and directly binds to NAC-responsive cis-elements (CACG and ABRE motifs) in the promoter of dammarenediol synthase (PgDDS), a key enzyme gene in the ginsenoside biosynthesis pathway, thereby activating its transcription. Overexpression of PgNAC72 in ginseng callus significantly increases total saponin content, particularly dammarane-type ginsenosides, as confirmed by transcriptomic and terpenoid metabolomic analyses. These findings elucidate a regulatory mechanism of MeJA-mediated ginsenoside biosynthesis and identify PgNAC72 as a promising target for metabolic engineering to enhance the medicinal value of P. ginseng.

science.title: The connotation of the "brain-gut-testis" axis and its application prospects in male reproductive diseases.
science.description: The kidney is the innate foundation, storing essence and generating marrow, and is responsible for reproduction. The brain is a sea of marrow, which was transformed by kidney essence, and also nourished by water and grain essence derived from the spleen and stomach. The spleen and stomach are the foundation of postnatal development, mainly responsible for receiving, transporting, and transforming water and grain essence. The functions of the large and small intestine are closely related to them. Male reproductive diseases are increasingly receiving attention. Inspired by the innate and acquired relationship in traditional Chinese medicine, the relationship between the brain and intestines, as well as the relationship between intestines and testes, based on scientific research progress in traditional Chinese medicine, it is believed that the brain, intestines, and testes interact to jointly maintain male reproductive health. So, the "brain-gut-testis" ais of male reproduction is condensed and proposed. Specifically, the brain regulates gastrointestinal and testicular functions through neuroendocrine mechanisms, and the gastrointestinal tract can afect brain and testicular function through gut microbiota, brain gut peptides and other factors, while testicles can afect gastrointestinal and brain function through androgens and other factors. The interaction between brain function, gastrointestinal function, and testicular reproductive function is coordinated physiologically and afects pathologically, jointly maintaining and afecting male reproductive health. [ABSTRACT FROM AUTHOR]

science.title: Decoding the landscape of cell-type-specific co-expressed transcription factors in soybean
science.description: Soybean (Glycine max) is an essential source of protein and oil with high nutritional value for human and animal consumption. To enhance our understanding of soybean biology, it is essential to have accurate information regarding the expression of each of its protein-coding genes. Here, we present Tabula Glycine max, a soybean single-cell resolution transcriptome atlas. This atlas comprises single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from ten different G. max organs and morphological structures constituting the entire soybean plant. These nuclei are grouped into 156 different clusters based on their transcriptomic profiles. The breadth of various organs, tissues and cell types represented in Tabula Glycine max reveals that the pattern of co-expressed transcription factor genes is sufficient to define most cell types based on their function and organ of origin. Defining cell-type-specific co-expressed transcription factor genes offers a new perspective to engineer cell-type-specific programmes and enhance the biology of unique soybean cell types. This cellular resolution and breadth make the Tabula Glycine max an exceptional resource for the plant and soybean communities. The soybean single-cell transcriptome atlas, Tabula Glycine max, spans ten organs. This resource reveals that the pattern of co-expressed transcription factor genes defines most cell types based on their function and organ of origin.
